paragraphs.text: Called also Abijah. {2Ch 12:16} Abijah signifieth, The Lord is my father: so his father called him, likely, with respect to that promise made to David; {2Sa 7:14} but because he walked not in the ways of David, therefore is Abijah called Abijam, which signifieth, My father is a sea. Indeed, Rehoboam was inconstant in good, wavering "like a wave of the sea driven by the wind and tossed." {Jas 1:6}
His mother’s name was Maachah.] Called also Micalah; {2Ch 13:2} we read likewise of a woman called Abijah. {2Ch 29:1}
Or, Absalom, whose daughter or niece by his daughter Tamar this Maachah may seem to have been: her husband’s name was Uriel of Gibeah. {2Ch 13:2}
Though at first he seemed to be somewhat good, {2Ch 13:12} yet soon after he showed himself in his colours.
paragraphs.anchor: And he walked in all the sins.

paragraphs.text: That is, In his sight, whereby he became an ill precedent to him.
paragraphs.anchor: Which he had done before him.

paragraphs.text: That is, A royal glory in a successor.
paragraphs.anchor: Did the Lord his God give him a lamp.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Of set purpose, against conseience, with any allowance and approbation. He had his other faults and failings, as his lies to Jonathan, {1Sa 20:6} to Ahimelech, {1Sa 21:2} to Achish, {1Sa 27:10} his unkindness to Mephibosheth, his polygamy, his fond sparing of his untoward sons, his numbering the people, &c. But as great virtues not sweetened with sincerity, are no ornament to men; so great infirmities not soured with hypocrisy, are no great deformities to them: those God acknowledgeth not; these he imputeth not.
paragraphs.anchor: And turned not aside from anything

paragraphs.text: There indeed he was false-hearted, and that kept him for a time from confessing it, and caused him to devise bad shifts to hide it; which doing one year, brought him many years of trouble.
paragraphs.anchor: Save only in the matter of Uriah.

paragraphs.text: See 1Ki 14:30.

Sharp wars, {2Ch 13:3} by a just hand of God upon both those kingdoms for their idolatry. And for like cause the dissensions between England and Scotland consumed more Christian blood, wrought more spoil and destruction, and continued longer than ever quarrel we read of did between any two people of the world.

This was a good king. But it is wonder how he should be good, of the seed of Abijam, of the soil of Maachah, both wicked, both idolatrous. Thus we have seen, saith a reverend man, a fair flower spring out of dung, and a well-fruited tree rise out of a sour stock.
See on 1Ki 14:31.

His father Abijam was soon cut off for his wickedness: Asa, that he might reform a state so far out of order, had a long reign granted him. Think the same of Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth. Asa reigned in Judah, in the times of the reigns of eight kings in Israel.
paragraphs.anchor: And forty and one years reigned he.

paragraphs.text: And his mother’s name was Maachah.] That is, His grandmother’s, who was a most wicked woman, nec tamen Asa mores eius retinuit, saith Vatablus, yet Asa kept himself uncorrupted by her, which was no small commendation. Pliny {a} praiseth young Quadratus, quod in deliciis aviae degens viveret tamen severisime, for that he lived strictly under the government of a loose grandmother.
{a} Epist., lib. vii.
Right, for the matter of his obedience; uprightly, for the manner.
paragraphs.anchor: And Asa did that which was right.

paragraphs.text: See 1Ki 14:24. How far from this zeal of good Asa was Pope Sixtus Quartus, qui lupanar utriusque Veneris Romae condidit, et tribus mensibus anni calidioribus, Iunio, Iulio, et Augusto, toti familiae Cardinalis Sanctae Luciae masculam venerem permisit cum Apostilla, Fiat ut petitur. {a} The Papists themselves write {b} with detestation, that in Rome a Jewish maid might not be admitted into the stews of whoredom, unless she would be first baptized.
paragraphs.anchor: And he took away the sodomites.

paragraphs.text: The dirty idols, the dunghill deities: {c} so called here, because of the stench wherewith they offend Almighty God.
{a} Corn. Agrippa.
{b} Espencaeus
{c} Deos stercores
Queen regent, or queen mother at least. Ne Domina esset, so the Tigurine; ne princeps esset in sacris Priapi, so the Vulgate; ne esset Augusta, so Junius; ne esset sacerdotissa prima, so others.

Heb., A horrible ugly thing, which some say was the picture of Priapus, others of Pan; others hold it to have been Idolum turpissimum a matre ad cultum Veneris institutum, a most filthy idol, set up in honour of Venus.
paragraphs.anchor: Because she had made an idol.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Cut off, deheaded it, as the expression is in Hos 10:2.

sc., Such as were set up for the worship of God; for as for those that were set up in honour of idols, he removed them. But he should have done both, as did afterwards zealous Hezekiah and Josiah. It is with the saints as with Jonathan’s signal arrows - two fell short, and but one beyond the mark; so where one shooteth home to the mark of the high calling in Christ Jesus, many fall short.
paragraphs.anchor: But the high places were not removed

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect.] With one breath doth God report both these; such is his indulgency. He will not see weakness where he seeth truth. All Asa’s infirmities are covered with the mantle of sincerity. Contrarily in Jehu, the Holy Ghost, after a description of many excellent things done by him, doth at last as it were draw a cross line. {2Ki 10:31}
viz., After his great victory over Jeroboam, {2Ch 13:15} though otherwise he were a wicked king.
paragraphs.anchor: And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated

paragraphs.text: See on 1Ki 14:30.
He sought to block him up, and so to keep his own people - who had a mind to the sincere service of God - from flying away to him.
paragraphs.anchor: That he might not suffer any.

paragraphs.text: This was plain sacrilege, since no necessity urged him thereunto.
paragraphs.anchor: Then Asa took all the silver.

paragraphs.text: And the treasures of the king’s house.] Which were much augmented doubtless by the great spoils of the Ethiopians and Lubims, lately beaten by him.
Alias Rezon, of whom see 1Ki 11:23.
Thus, through unbelief, he basely beggeth help of an idolater.

Though against his oath. The Turks’ leagues, grounded upon the law of nations, be they with never so strong capitulations concluded, or solemnity of oath confirmed, have with them no longer force than standeth with their own profit. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: So Benhadad hearkened unto king Asa.

paragraphs.text: {a} Turk Hist., pref.
Seeking no further revenge against Asa.
Where also he had made a great pit or trench, for fear of Baasha. {Jer 41:9}

He that imprisoned the prophet is imprisoned in his bed; there being more pain in those fetters put by God upon Asa than in those put by Asa upon Hanani. This good man was the worse a while for whipping.
paragraphs.anchor: He was diseased in his feet.

paragraphs.text: Sic uno avulso non deficit alter Aureus.
Two years peaceably, and eight years in affliction, saith Vatablus; but the truth is, he reigned not two full years in all. {1Ki 15:28}
paragraphs.anchor: And reigned over Israel two years.

paragraphs.text: See on 1Ki 14:23.
Sed quo iure? They had gotten it; but the right of it was in Israel. {Jos 21:23}
Casting out his body to the dogs to be devoured, as Ahijah had forethreatened.
The fulfilling whereof Baasha aimed not at; but the wise God effected it. The devil and his imps do God’s will, though oft against their own will.
paragraphs.anchor: According to the saying of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Sin is the mother of misery. Jeroboam by idolatry thought to have established his kingdom, but he ruined it.
